comments.content: [medium] The lambda `time_t_to_string` is declared inside the loop body, so it gets re-created on every iteration. Since it captures nothing from the surrounding scope, hoisting it out of the loop — or making it a static helper function — would improve performance.

[medium] Every TTLDelete scheduling goes through this `LOG_TRACE`, which builds a time string using `ostringstream`/`put_time`. Even with TRACE normally off, the logger implementation may still evaluate the arguments, adding avoidable overhead. Where your logging framework supports it, wrap the construction in `if (log->isTraceEnabled())` (or an equivalent check), or switch to a lazy/formatting helper that does no work when the level is disabled.
[low] A small test for the alternate `MergeTreeDataMergerMutator` branch would make this path less fragile.
